questions.question: The opening command of Surah Al-Maidah, 'fulfill all contracts,' uses the Arabic word uqud. What does the tafsir say this word encompasses?
options: Only commercial business contracts between Muslim merchants
Only the covenant between a person and Allah as described in the Quran
Every binding agreement: the covenant with Allah, agreements between people, and all social and commercial contracts
Exclusively the tribal peace treaties made during the early Medinan period
questions.explanation: Imam Tabari records that Ibn Abbas held uqud refers to divine covenants, but the majority position endorsed by Tabari himself is that the term is general, covering every category of covenant and contract — with Allah, between people, and in social and commercial life.

questions.question: Verse 1 of Al-Maidah permits hunting while a person is in the state of ihram for Hajj or Umrah.
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly forbids it: 'other than those hunting while you are in a state of ihram.' According to hadith in Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, a muhrim who kills game owes a compensatory sacrifice, making hunting during ihram clearly prohibited.

questions.question: Ibn Kathir explains that the verse prohibiting violation of sha'air Allah was partly revealed in relation to a specific historical situation. What was that situation?
options: A group of Muslim traders were attacked in Makkah during the pilgrimage season
Some Muslims considered attacking polytheists traveling to Makkah for pilgrimage — the same people who had blocked Muslims from the Sacred Mosque
The Prophet forbade Muslims from trading with pilgrims arriving from non-Muslim tribes
Certain companions were found hunting within the boundaries of the Sacred Mosque
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir records that this verse was revealed partly in relation to polytheists traveling to Makkah for pilgrimage whom some Muslims considered attacking, since those same people had blocked Muslims from the Sacred Mosque. The verse prohibited this, affirming universal protection for the pilgrimage season.

questions.question: Sayyid Qutb described the Quranic command not to let enmity drive one to injustice as one of the highest moral achievements in human civilization.
questions.explanation: In Fi Zilal al-Quran, Sayyid Qutb calls this instruction one of the highest moral achievements in human civilization, arguing that it transcends tribal and national psychology by demanding Muslims maintain justice even toward enemies who actively harmed them.

questions.question: On which occasion do Sunni classical scholars most widely report that the verse of perfection — 'Today I have perfected your religion' — was revealed?
options: The night of the Prophet's migration from Makkah to Madinah
The Day of Arafah during the Farewell Pilgrimage, which fell on a Friday
The day of the conquest of Makkah when the Prophet entered the Sacred Mosque
The day of the Battle of Badr
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir records that Umar ibn al-Khattab confirmed this verse was revealed on the Day of Arafah, a Friday, while the Prophet stood at that sacred place during the Farewell Pilgrimage. A Jewish scholar's comment that this day would have been celebrated as a festival prompted Umar's reply.

questions.question: Wahbah al-Zuhayli noted in Al-Tafsir al-Munir that the wisdom behind dietary prohibitions such as carrion and blood has been confirmed by which modern field?
options: Ancient Greek medical texts later incorporated into Islamic jurisprudence
Modern microbiology and medicine, which confirm dead animals and blood are vectors for dangerous pathogens
Economic studies showing that trading in these items destabilizes food markets
Comparative religion research showing all Abrahamic faiths share identical restrictions
questions.explanation: Al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir notes that modern microbiology and medicine confirm carrion and blood are vectors for dangerous pathogens, and that the prohibition of swine's flesh is supported by research on parasites such as Trichinella spiralis — welcome additional benefits beyond the spiritual purpose.

questions.question: Imam al-Qurtubi derived from the emergency concession in verse 3 the fiqhi principle that necessity makes the prohibited permissible, strictly limited to the extent of preserving life.
questions.explanation: In Al-Jami li-Ahkam al-Quran, Imam al-Qurtubi extensively analyzed the phrase 'whoever is forced by severe hunger without inclining to sin,' establishing the principle al-darura tubih al-mahzurat — necessity makes the prohibited permissible — but limited strictly to preserving life without willful sin.

questions.question: Verse 5 permits Muslim men to marry chaste women from the People of the Book under specific conditions. Which condition is explicitly mentioned in the verse itself?
options: The woman must study Islamic jurisprudence for one year before the marriage
The local Muslim community must give collective approval to the marriage
The husband must provide the mahr and the marriage must be one of chastity, not illicit relations
The couple must reside in a Muslim-majority country
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly conditions the permission on providing due compensation (mahr) and on the union being one of chastity — not fornication or the taking of secret lovers. Al-Qurtubi notes scholars unanimously restrict the permission to free, chaste women of the People of the Book.

questions.question: Imam Tabari's Jami al-Bayan documents a classical scholarly debate about the word 'arjulakum' (your feet) in the wudu verse. What was the nature of that debate?
options: Whether feet had to be washed in running water or if still water was sufficient
Whether the word's grammatical case ending indicated washing or wiping, resolved by the Sunni majority in favour of washing the feet
Whether the obligation to wash feet applied only to men or also to women
Whether the ankle bones were to be included in or excluded from the washing
questions.explanation: Tabari records the linguistic debate over whether 'arjulakum' carries a case ending suggesting washing or wiping. The Sunni scholarly majority resolved this in favour of washing the feet, consistent with the hadith in Sahih Bukhari from Abu Hurayrah that prayer is invalid without valid wudu.

questions.question: According to the tafsir of verse 6, the permission to perform tayammum with clean earth when water is unavailable was preceded by a real incident involving the Companion Aisha and a lost necklace during a journey.
questions.explanation: The most frequently cited sabab al-nuzul for the tayammum portion of verse 6 involves Aisha, whose necklace was lost during a journey, causing the caravan to halt in a waterless place. This incident prompted the revelation permitting dry ablution, recorded in both Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.

questions.question: Sayyid Qutb reflected on the closing phrase of the wudu verse, 'that you may be grateful.' What spiritual significance did he draw from this phrase?
options: It shows gratitude is an obligatory condition for the validity of wudu
The entire framework of purification is designed to awaken in the believer a consciousness of divine blessing with every prayer
It confirms that Allah will reward each act of wudu with a specific blessing in the Hereafter
It establishes that cleanliness is the highest virtue in Islam
questions.explanation: In Fi Zilal al-Quran, Sayyid Qutb argues that 'la'allakum tashkurun' shows the purification framework is designed to awaken consciousness of divine blessing with every prayer, making wudu an act of worship and gratitude — not mere hygiene — that links the body's preparation to internal renewal of intention.

questions.question: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi interpreted the instruction 'enter through the gate' in verse 23 as a principle that one must exhaust all available practical means before placing reliance on Allah for the outcome.
questions.explanation: Al-Razi in Mafatih al-Ghayb explains that 'enter through the gate' teaches a principle formalised in Islamic jurisprudence: one must take all practical means (asbab) first. He states there is no genuine tawakkul without exhausting proper means, and that action and tawakkul are inseparable for the believer.

questions.question: In the Cain and Abel story, what did Abel mean when he told Cain 'I want you to obtain my sin and your sin'?
options: He was cursing Cain and demanding divine retribution
By refusing to retaliate, Abel ensured Cain would bear the full burden of unjust murder alone, rather than Abel sharing guilt through a counter-killing
He was admitting a previous personal sin and asking Cain to bear responsibility for it
He was explaining a Torah ruling that transferred guilt between brothers
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir and Imam Tabari explain that Abel was not expressing vindictiveness. By not retaliating, he allowed Cain to bear the undivided, full guilt of unjust murder. Had Abel killed Cain defensively, he would have shared that guilt; by surrendering, Cain alone carries the complete burden.

questions.question: Ibn Kathir cites a hadith from Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim narrated by Ibn Masud that links Cain's murder to all subsequent unjust killings. What does that hadith say?
options: That the one who starts a bad practice bears the sin of all who follow it, narrated by Abu Hurayrah
That no soul is wrongfully killed except that Cain bears a share of that sin, because he was the first to establish murder in the world
That murder is the sin that most pollutes the earth, narrated by Umar ibn al-Khattab
That major sins committed by earlier nations transfer their weight to Muslims who imitate them
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir explicitly references the hadith from Ibn Masud in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim: the Prophet said no soul is wrongfully killed except that Cain (the first son of Adam) bears a share of that sin, because he was the one who first established the practice of murder in the world.

questions.question: Sayyid Qutb described verse 30's phrase 'his soul permitted to him the murder' as which of the following?
options: Evidence that free will does not exist and humans are compelled by their nature
A masterpiece of psychological and moral narration showing that sin is rarely a single decision but the end product of a soul slowly groomed by unchecked desires
A description of Cain being spiritually possessed, which overrode his will
An illustration of how peer pressure in a corrupt society drives individuals to violence
questions.explanation: In Fi Zilal al-Quran, Sayyid Qutb calls verse 30 a masterpiece of psychological and moral narration. He argues the Quran shows that sin is rarely a single dramatic decision but the end product of a soul gradually groomed by unchecked desires — which is why Islam places such emphasis on tawbah and active discipline of the nafs.

questions.question: Narrations recorded by Imam Tabari from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud state that Cain buried Abel immediately upon seeing a dead bird on the ground.
questions.explanation: Tabari records from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud that Cain carried his brother's body on his back for an extended time, bewildered about what to do, until Allah sent a crow. Only after watching the crow scratch the earth to bury another dead crow did Cain learn the practice of burial and cry out in remorse.

questions.question: Verse 32, immediately following the Cain and Abel story, establishes a universal principle about human life. Which statement best captures both sides of that principle?
options: The state must execute murderers and reward those who prevent crime
Killing one innocent person is as if killing all of humanity, and saving one life is as if saving all of humanity
Only blood relatives of the victim have standing to seek retribution or offer pardon
Witnesses to a murder who do not intervene share equally in the guilt of the killer
questions.explanation: Verse 32, decreed for the Children of Israel and understood as a universal principle, establishes the infinite weight of each human life in both directions: unjust killing of one person equals killing all of humanity, while saving one person equals saving all of humanity, affirming the sacred status of every human soul.

questions.question: Wahbah al-Zuhayli argued in Al-Tafsir al-Munir that the miracles of each prophet were calibrated to challenge the dominant expertise of their era. What does he say about Jesus's miracles specifically?
options: They were identical to Moses's miracles to show the unity of prophetic mission
They were primarily literary miracles to challenge the poetry of the time
They were medical in nature — healing the blind, lepers, and raising the dead — because healing arts were highly valued in Jesus's era
They were political miracles designed to challenge the authority of Roman rule
questions.explanation: Al-Zuhayli observes in Al-Tafsir al-Munir that miracles were calibrated to the dominant expertise of each age: Moses overcame Egyptian mastery of magic, Muhammad's miracle was the inimitable Quran in an age of Arabic eloquence, and Jesus's miracles were medical because healing arts were most valued and contested in his time.

questions.question: Ibn Kathir explains that Jesus's use of the word 'Eid' in his prayer for the heavenly table comes from an Arabic root meaning 'to return,' indicating a day people return to repeatedly in commemoration.
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir explains that the word 'Eid' derives from the root 'awada' meaning to return, suggesting a recurring day of commemoration. He links this to the early Islamic usage of the term for Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, noting that Tabari records how some Christian communities preserved a corrupted echo of this original event.

questions.question: On the Day of Judgment in verse 116, Allah asks Jesus whether he commanded people to worship him and his mother as two gods. What is the opening of Jesus's response?
options: He remains silent and defers entirely to Allah without offering a reply
He begins with 'Subhanaka' (Exalted are You!) and states it was not for him to say what he had no right to say
He asks Allah to forgive his followers for misunderstanding his message
He confirms he said it but explains it was a metaphor misunderstood by later generations
questions.explanation: Jesus opens his response in verse 116 with 'Subhanaka' — a declaration of divine transcendence — and states it was not for him to say that to which he had no right. Wahbah al-Zuhayli notes this demolishes any claim to divinity, as Jesus firmly places himself in the station of servitude rather than lordship.

questions.question: Ibn Kathir cites a hadith from Sahih Muslim and Sahih Bukhari in which the Prophet recited verse 118 alongside the similar prayer of Prophet Ibrahim. What did the Prophet do upon reciting these two verses?
options: He commanded his companions to memorise them as the greatest supplications in the Quran
He raised his hands in supplication and wept for his ummah, demonstrating prophetic concern and humility before Allah's judgment
He declared a day of fasting to mourn the corruption of earlier communities
He recited them as part of a special night prayer reserved for times of communal difficulty
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir records a hadith in Sahih Muslim and Sahih Bukhari where the Prophet recited verse 118 alongside Ibrahim's prayer (14:36), then raised his hands in supplication and wept for his ummah — a profound moment illustrating that prophets submit entirely to Allah's judgment regarding their communities.

questions.question: The majority position among classical Sunni scholars — including Ibn Kathir, Tabari, and al-Qurtubi — is that the heavenly table (al-maidah) actually descended in response to Jesus's prayer.
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir, Tabari, and al-Qurtubi all maintain that the table did descend, based on the apparent meaning of Allah's direct promise in verse 115 ('Indeed, I will send it down to you'). Tabari records from Abdullah ibn Amr that those who disbelieved after witnessing it will receive the most severe punishment on the Day of Resurrection.
